captions.detailed: This 3D model is a single, flat, rectangular link arm designed for a scissor lift mechanism. It has fully rounded semicircular ends, giving it a sleek obround shape. Along its length, there is a series of circular holes: a larger pivot hole at each end, one larger pivot hole in the exact center, and four smaller adjustment holes evenly spaced on either side of the center hole.
captions.instruction: Create a parametric scissor lift leg in OpenSCAD. The user should be able to adjust the overall leg length, the width and thickness of the bar, the diameter of the main pivot holes (located at both ends and the center), and the number and diameter of the smaller intermediate holes spaced between the pivots.
captions.factory: The code defines a module `scissorLiftLeg` which uses a `difference()` operation. The main bar shape is constructed by applying `hull()` to two `cylinder` primitives translated to opposite ends of the leg length. It then subtracts three main pivot cylinders (one at each end and one in the center). A `for` loop is used to calculate the positions and subtract the smaller intermediate cylinders on both halves of the leg.
